title: Pentanuclear Dysprosium Hydroxy Cluster Showing Single-Molecule-Magnet Behavior

synthesis.procedure: DyCl3·6H2O (1.00 g, 2.65 mmol) and dibenzoylmethane (Ph2acacH, 1.19 g, 5.30 mmol) were dissolved in 50 mL of ethanol, and triethylamine (1.5 mL, 1.09 g, 10.79 mmol) was added. The mixture was heated to reflux for 10 min and then stirred at room temperature overnight. The precipitate was filtered and washed ten times with 10 mL of ethanol. Large yellow crystals of 1 were obtained overnight by crystallization from a hot ethanol/CH2Cl2/hexane mixture (1:3:10). Recrystallization from toluene also gave crystals of 1, but of poorer X-ray quality.

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Precipitate filtered and washed ten times with 10 mL ethanol. Large yellow crystals grown overnight from hot ethanol/CH2Cl2/hexane (1:3:10).

properties.summary: Compound 1 is an SMM: dc χT is 63 cm3 K mol−1 at 300 K (1000 Oe), decreasing to 31.0 cm3 K mol−1 at 1.81 K. Curie–Weiss fit above 1.8 K gives C = 63.2 cm3 K mol−1 and θ = −3.5 K, indicating weak antiferromagnetic interactions and/or crystal-field effects. No M vs H hysteresis above 1.8 K. Slow magnetization relaxation appears below ~3–8 K; Arrhenius analysis of ac data (1.8–3.6 K, zero dc field) gives Ueff/kB = 33 K and τ0 ≈ 4.5 × 10−9 s. A small dc field slightly speeds relaxation, suggesting no quantum tunneling above 1.8 K.
